read:tracing.summary: Perfetto tracing is enabled through runtron's --trace / --trace-gen / --trace-passes flags or the perfetto/tronperf launcher (which runs runtron with --trace traced). The tree has a main-thread span "convert_k_blocks" (new in PR 4901, carries the block count) and a per-layer "Save K" span, but nothing wraps the note_k_row_saved loop or a page visit; the finest attention span is one per apply_page_range call. TRON_ATTN_STATS (attn_stats.hpp) is present: it counts visits and K tokens per path (empty/avx/amx) and keeps per-job busy cycles, but it has no per-path cycle counter and one "avx" visit covers both the qk_group reader and the row-major dotter tail, so it cannot split those two. The cheapest probe is rdtsc() pairs from h/system/system.hpp at three sites (convert loop, note loop, software loop) with accumulators printed at exit in the page_share exit_reporter pattern or added to attn_stats rows. perf exists on delphi-3bda per the memory note (perf 6.8.12, sudo -n needed, not re-verified here); the build keeps frame pointers and DWARF-4 line info, so perf record -g gives call chains and per-source-line attribution inside the always_inline apply_page_tok, but only on a build-tree binary (the .deb is stripped).

facts.claim: runtron has three Perfetto flags: --trace FILE|traced (whole run), --trace-gen FILE|traced (phased: starts at prompt-parse completion), and --trace-passes SPEC (requires --trace-gen; gates application track events to the selected 1-based forward passes, 0 = startup).
facts.evidence: src/runtron.cpp:94-97 (option strings), :544-575 (harvest: trace-passes requires trace-gen; --trace sets tracing; --trace-gen sets phased_tracing), README.perfetto.md section 'perfetto/tronperf' bullets on --trace-passes and TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN

facts.claim: An in-process file capture (--trace FILE or --trace-gen FILE without --trace-passes) is capped at 5 s (perfetto_duration_ms = 5*1000) because start_tracing's legacy_local_duration defaults to true; the --trace-passes path calls start_tracing(dest, false) and has no cap; a 'traced' destination uses the daemon config instead (runtron.cfg: duration_ms 800000, 1 GiB ring buffer for track events, streamed to file every 500 ms).
facts.evidence: src/pos/perf.cpp:33 'const int perfetto_duration_ms = 5 * 1000;', :135 'if (legacy_duration) config.set_duration_ms(perfetto_duration_ms);', :146-180 (traced branch vs in-process branch); h/common/perfetto.hpp:261 'void start_tracing(std::string_view trace_dest, bool legacy_local_duration = true);'; src/runtron.cpp:267 'start_tracing(tron::perfetto_trace_dest, false)' (trace-passes path) vs :336 'tron::start_tracing(trace_dest)'; perfetto/runtron.cfg lines 1-12 and 40-45

facts.claim: The launcher perfetto/tronperf always runs runtron with --trace traced (or --trace-gen traced with --gen), starts traced and traced_probes, and writes the trace to --output-file; the invocation is 'nix run .#tronperf -- --output-file F [--gen] [runtron args...]'.
facts.evidence: README.perfetto.md 'Quick Start' block and the note 'perfetto/tronperf always runs runtron with --trace traced (or --trace-gen traced with --gen)'; perfetto/tronperf lines 90-140 (option parsing; --trace/--trace-gen rejected before --)

facts.claim: Every TRACE_EVENT in tron is gated twice: the SDK category-enabled check and tron's application_track_events_enabled(); with no session open the macro costs the category check only. Perfetto's TraceMuxer thread is pinned to core 0 by runtron so it does not share a core with the main thread.

answers.question: (1) How to enable a Perfetto trace of a runtron run (flag/env, output file, cost)?
answers.answer: Two routes. Route A, the launcher: run 'nix run .#tronperf -- --output-file /path/run.trace --gen --trace-passes 300-340 -m qwen-3-4b ... -l 256' inside the checkout. tronperf starts traced and traced_probes, passes '--trace-gen traced' to gen/runtron, and the daemon writes --output-file. '--trace-passes' needs --trace-gen and gates application events to the chosen forward passes (0 = startup, so prefill can be isolated with '1' for the prompt pass, and decode steady state with a late range). TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN=N is the older way to skip the first tokens. Route B, in-process: 'gen/runtron --trace-gen /path/run.trace --trace-passes 300-340 ...' writes the file itself; categories then come from TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES (for example '-*,+model'). Without --trace-passes an in-process capture stops after 5 s (perfetto_duration_ms). Cost: the memory category measured within 0.2 % of untraced; the memory note from the router work measured a full trace at about 19 % lower TPS and channel waits inflated about 2.5x. So a trace gives structure (which spans, how many, in which thread) and relative sizes, and every magnitude used in a verdict must be re-measured untraced. For the H3 question the trace is cheap in events: 'convert_k_blocks' is one span per forward and 'Save K' is one per layer per thread.

answers.question: (2) Which existing spans attribute H3 (convert_k_blocks) and save_k time per layer; is there a span around the attention worker loop or per page visit?
answers.answer: H3: TRACE_EVENT("model", "convert_k_blocks", "blocks", N) [model.hpp:3178], main thread, once per forward, after wait_for_coop_gof and before logit delivery [model.hpp:1840-1847]; the 'blocks' argument is the queue length, so the trace gives both ns per step and blocks per step directly. Save K: TRACE_EVENT("model", "Save K") [model.hpp:3367] covers the whole save_k_impl of one layer on the main thread (and one span per helper when the store is shared). It includes the note_k_row_saved loop [model.hpp:3425-3437] but does not isolate it; a nested span would be needed for that. Attention: the finest span is per apply_page_range call ('Attention Ready' / 'Attention Pending', with layer, kv head, thread, q range) [self_attention.hpp:1487-1497]; there is no span around run_attention_job (only rdtsc timers at :813-845) and none per page visit. A per-visit span would be too fine: about 36,864 visits per user per decode step at prompt 8192 (36 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 pages).
answers.evidence: h/tron/models/model.hpp:1840-1847, :3176-3182, :3364-3367, :3425-3437; h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:775-860, :1152-1175, :1487-1497, :1279; grep TRACE_EVENT output for self_attention.hpp

answers.question: (3) Is TRON_ATTN_STATS available in this tree, does it count visits per path and cycles, and can it split qk_group from the dotter tail?
answers.answer: Yes, it is in the tree (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp, included by self_attention.hpp:28, state at :465-493). Switch: environment variable TRON_ATTN_STATS exactly '1'. It counts visits and K tokens per path (empty, avx, amx) per (class, pool worker, layer, ready/pending pass), plus avx_full_page_visits, and it keeps cycle timers T1-T5 (forward wall, per-job busy, job wall on worker 0, layer period, join wait). There is no cycle counter per path, and one avx visit covers both k_vnni::qk_group on the VNNI blocks and the row-major dotter tail of the same page (attn_stats.hpp:112-118; self_attention.hpp:2027-2050 then one return at :2087). So it cannot split the software loop between qk_group and the dotter tail. What it can give for Issue 4934: a kill-switch vs AMX-on comparison of busy_cycles (T2) per layer and of avx_full_page_visits, and a PR 4898 vs PR 4901 comparison of T2 per layer under the kill switch (same visit counts, different time). For batch runtron the stderr '[attn-stats]' report at state destruction is the output; the FUSE leaves need fuse::stats initialized.

answers.question: (4) Cheapest instrumentation for a probe build: (a) ns per step in convert_pending_k_blocks and block count; (b) ns per layer in the note_k_row_saved loop; (c) ns per step in the software loop for row-major rows vs qk_group.
answers.answer: Helpers: tron::hardware::system::rdtsc() [h/system/system.hpp:317-321], cycles_to_ns(uint64_t) [h/system/system.hpp:269-276, asserts calibration done] and get_cpu_freq() [h/system/system.hpp:338; 0 before calibration]. Existing idiom: 'uint64_t x = 0; x -= rdtsc(); work; x += rdtsc();' [self_attention.hpp:813-819; llama.hpp:660, :694]. Exit print pattern: inline std::atomic<uint64_t> totals plus 'struct exit_reporter { ~exit_reporter() { fprintf(stderr, ...); } }; inline exit_reporter report_at_exit;' [h/tron/kernels/page_share_counters.hpp:37-62, :118-151]; convert cycles with cycles_to_ns at print time only. (a) In convert_pending_k_blocks [model.hpp:3176-3182]: main thread only, so plain statics suffice: 'static uint64_t h3_cycles, h3_calls, h3_blocks;' then 'h3_cycles -= rdtsc(); for (...) k_block_to_vnni_at(...); h3_cycles += rdtsc(); h3_calls++; h3_blocks += pending_k_blocks_.size();'. Cost 2 rdtsc per forward. Print ns per forward = cycles_to_ns(h3_cycles)/h3_calls and blocks per forward. (b) In save_k_impl around the block at model.hpp:3425-3437 (main thread only, helpers returned at :3395-3398): 'static uint64_t note_cycles[MAX_LAYERS], note_calls[MAX_LAYERS], note_pushes[MAX_LAYERS];' indexed by layer.i; same rdtsc pair; cost 2 rdtsc per layer per minibatch (72 per step for 36 layers, under 1 us est.). Also take a pair at :3367 (after the Save K TRACE_EVENT) to :3455 to get the whole main-thread save_k per layer, so the note loop can be read as a fraction. (c) Worker side, inside apply_page_tok [self_attention.hpp:1856-2088]; this runs on every attention worker so per-worker accumulators are required. Cheapest and consistent with the tree: add four fields to attn_stats::worker_layer_row (tail_rows, tail_cycles, qk_calls, qk_cycles) and four to visit_tally, gate on the existing stats_enabled bool and flush through the existing add_visits [self_attention.hpp:1475-1483, :1676-1681; attn_stats.hpp:198-247], print in print_report. Timestamps: t0 before the dotter construction at :1969 (PR 4901 pays it on every visit; the lazy probe does not), t1 after the token loop ends at :2039, t2 after qk_group at :2050; tail_cycles += t1 - t0 only when the tail branch at :2029 fired at least once (count tail_rows there), else attribute t1 - t0 to a third bucket 'loop_other_cycles'; qk_cycles += t2 - t1 when live != 0. That is 3 rdtsc per visit with relevant tokens; 3 x ~25 cycles = ~75 cycles est. against a 64-token qk_group of 32,768 multiply-adds, so a few percent est. on the software loop itself, which is of the same order as the 2.7-3.7 % effect under study. Two ways to keep the distortion below the effect: (i) count always (tail_rows, qk_calls, pages with a tail: one integer add each) and time only every 16th visit (use stats_tally.n_visits & 15), scaling by 16 in the report; (ii) time at apply_page_range granularity only (one pair per call around the loop at :1526-1675, same place as the existing TRACE_EVENT) and read the split from the counts. Report both: counts per step and sampled ns per step per path. Because the tail timer brackets the dotter construction too, running the same probe on worktree P (lazy dotters) isolates the construction cost.

answers.question: (5) Is perf available on delphi-3bda for a perf record of runtron, and would perf record -g on the engine for 30 s of decode give per-function attribution given the inlining?
answers.answer: The memory note from 2026-09-17 says perf 6.8.12 is on delphi-3bda (kernel 6.8.0-138), needs 'sudo -n' because perf_event_paranoid is 4, and was used per-process with '-p <PID>' for EXE.AMX_BUSY; this was not re-verified in this session (no ssh, per the brief). A 'sudo -n perf record -g -p <engine pid> -- sleep 30' would work mechanically: all targets compile and link with -fno-omit-frame-pointer and -gdwarf-4 [CMakeLists.txt:572-573] and the native and deb presets are RelWithDebInfo [CMakePresets.json:37, :63], so frame-pointer call chains resolve and DWARF line tables are present. Two limits. First, the hot functions are always_inline (apply_page_tok is TRON(inline) = always_inline [attributes.hpp:78]) and runtron plus the model libraries use thin LTO [src/CMakeLists.txt:91; src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:270, :359, :369], so symbol-level 'perf report' will put the dotter tail, qk_group and the softmax step under one apply_page_range (or run_sections) instantiation; the split needs source-line attribution ('perf report --sort sym,srcline', 'perf annotate -l') or inlined-frame expansion ('perf report --inline', available in perf 6.8), which rely on the DWARF-4 info. Second, the installed .deb is stripped (CPACK_STRIP_FILES TRUE [CMakeLists.txt:811]), so the profile must target a build-tree gen/runtron or gen-deb/runtron, not /opt/positron. For H3 specifically perf is coarse: convert_pending_k_blocks is one short main-thread call per forward, so its samples are few; the rdtsc pair in (4a) is the better instrument, and perf is better used to compare the worker-side line profile of PR 4898 vs PR 4901 under the kill switch. Exact perf feature support on 3bda's binary: Insufficient data; 'perf report --help | grep inline' on 3bda would resolve it.

read:hwpath.summary: The hardware/software split is fixed once per model state at construction (cached_operation_uses_hw reads an array filled right after configure_hw_attention), so a lost shard (HBM exhausted), a prompt below the 127-token engagement point, or an empty per-batch hardware plan never flips an operation back to "software-scored": its blocks stay row-major forever and the software loop scores them with the row-major dotter. The FPGA staging gather (gof::populate via page_info::k_head_fn) runs only for KV slots in the hardware slot mask, which under hardware eligibility is exactly the set of hardware-scored operations, so for a software-scored operation no staging gather can ever read its pages and the "convert after wait_for_coop_gof" ordering is defensive, not required. Under the measured cells (TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 with USE_HW_ATTN=0) no hardware path is active at all: no shards, no GALs/GOFs, empty gof_jobs_span, null gof_rodeo_fn, wait_for_coop_gof returns at once, and every short-run block is recorded and converted on the main thread at the forward end. Under the FPGA path with every operation hardware-scored (qwen-3-4b has no sliding window), pending_k_blocks_ stays empty and convert_pending_k_blocks returns on its first line. A fix must keep: the 4-line row-major store for short runs, the in-place row return in k_head_fn, no conversion of hardware-scored operations' blocks, and a software loop that still handles row-major blocks scattered anywhere in the history (the page already carries a 4-bit per-page block mask, so no new mask is needed).

answers.question: (1) When does cached_operation_uses_hw(op) hold; once per operation or per minibatch/pass; what happens on 'lose HW attention'?
answers.answer: It holds iff the model state was built with hw_attn_eligible true (devices present, USE_HW_ATTN not 0 or model default on, shape eligible, EMEM fits a shard) and the operation is a hardware candidate with no sliding window (scale uniformity is guaranteed by eligibility). It is decided exactly once, in the model-state constructor (configure_hw_attention, then cache_attention_operation_hardware_eligibility fills attention_operation_uses_hw); nothing rewrites the array, so it never flips per minibatch or per pass. Losing HW attention (HBM exhausted: a 1024-token shard with sw_fallback, scored on the CPU), a prompt below the 127-token engagement point, or an empty per-batch hardware plan do not change it: the operation still counts as hardware-scored, save_k records no row bits for it, its decode-completed blocks stay row-major, and the software loop (driven by the sw_required mask for that range) scores those tokens with the row-major dotter (4 lines per token) while whole-block prefill blocks are read by k_vnni::qk_group. The shard note states this split is deliberately static: 'decided once per attention operation for a whole batch, while residency is per shard'.

answers.question: (2) Which thread gathers K rows for the GOF staging, for which operations, can an earlier minibatch's gather still read pages of a software-scored operation, and is the forward-end ordering needed for software-scored operations?
answers.answer: Gather chain: credit_gof_save (main thread, in save_k/save_v after the stores) enqueues a completed GOF; fire_gof_rodeo -> gof_rodeo_impl -> gof::prepare_for_dma -> gof::populate calls page_info::k_head_fn for 4 tokens x n_kv_heads. Drainers: attention workers via help_drain_gof(budget 4) in begin_attention_job (only the handwritten llama plugin at llama.hpp:754 and tests call it; generated plugins use run_attention_job which has no drain call), and the main thread in wait_for_coop_gof at the forward end; backfill_shard also populates, on the scheduler thread outside the forward. Operations: gof_rodeo_impl returns unless slot_uses_hw(slot), and GOFs exist only for slots in the hardware mask; that mask is set for exactly the candidate-and-no-sliding-window operations, the same predicate that makes cached_operation_uses_hw true once hw_attn_eligible holds. So a software-scored operation's KV slot is never staged (unless two operations share one slot, which was not verified), and no gather of an earlier minibatch can read rows that this pass records: rows are recorded only for software-scored operations (3425) and gathered only for hardware-scored ones. The forward-end ordering 'convert after wait_for_coop_gof' is therefore not required by any staging reader; it is defensive. What the forward-end placement still provides is 'after run() joined its workers'; the Note claims attention workers are not a reader of a block during its completing save because pending pages are read only after every writing minibatch counted its latch down (upstream_kvs_ready.wait at self_attention.hpp:821-823; save_k counts down at its end, model.hpp:3455-3457). Whether a page written in this pass can appear in a 'ready' section was not verified here.

answers.question: (3) Under the kill switch with USE_HW_ATTN=0 (the measured cells), is any hardware path active (gof, staging)?
answers.answer: No. USE_HW_ATTN=0 makes fwd_hw_attn_enabled return false, configure_hw_attention takes its disabled branch (hw_attn_eligible stays false, hw_kv_slots stays the empty default), so the scheduler creates no shards, no GALs/GOFs, passes empty hw_plan_entries, an empty gof_jobs_span and a null gof_rodeo_fn. In the model, cached_operation_uses_hw is false for every operation, so every short-run block is recorded (one atomic per token per layer per pass) and converted on the main thread at the forward end (for qwen-3-4b: 36 blocks x 8 KV heads = 288 block_to_vnni calls per user per 16 decode steps, computed from the Note's per-block figures). The only hardware remnants on the path are credit_gof_save's empty-span early return per (token, layer) in save_k and save_v, and wait_for_coop_gof finding an empty queue. The attention loop runs with uses_hw=false, i.e. run_visible_in_software, visiting every visible token.

answers.question: (4) In a mixed deployment (FPGA attention on), how often does the software loop score row-major blocks with the dotter per 1024-token shard, and does a fix that removes the per-token layout test need a mask of row-major blocks per page?
answers.answer: A software-scored range under a hardware operation (a degraded shard's 1024 tokens, positions below the engagement point, the causal tail above the DMA'd prefix) is visited every decode step by every query whose sw mask covers it, for every layer and KV head: 16 page visits per (query, layer, KV head) per shard, each walking up to 64 tokens, i.e. up to 1024 x 36 x 8 = 294,912 per-token bit tests per query per step for one fully-relevant degraded shard on qwen-3-4b (arithmetic from constants, not measured). Which of those tokens are row-major: every token saved by a run shorter than 16 (every decode token and a prompt's last partial block), permanently, because hardware-scored operations never queue a conversion; whole-block prefill tokens are VNNI and go through qk_group. The page already keeps the needed mask: page::k_vnni_blocks is one uint8_t per slot with one bit per 16-token block, fetched once per page visit (self_attention.hpp:2020-2022); the per-token test is a bit test on that register value. A fix can iterate per block from that 4-bit mask, so no new per-page mask is needed. What a fix must not assume is that row-major blocks sit only in the newest page's tail block: under hardware attention they are scattered through the whole decode history, so the row-major dotter path (or an equivalent row-major reader) must remain for any block whose bit is clear.

answers.question: (5) Under the FPGA path, does anything in the forward end (convert_pending_k_blocks) run at all (queue empty)? What must a fix keep unchanged to preserve PR #4901's FPGA gains (issue #4500)?
answers.answer: For a model whose operations are all hardware-scored (qwen-3-4b: no sliding window; candidate status per layer is declared by the plugin and was not read here), pending_k_blocks_ is never pushed (gate at model.hpp:3425) and convert_pending_k_blocks returns on its first line (3177); wait_for_coop_gof still runs and drains the tail of the GOF queue on main. Models with software-scored operations (sliding-window layers) still queue and convert those blocks. To keep the issue-#4500 gains a fix must keep: (a) short-run K rows stored row-major as 4 whole 64-byte lines (store_row_major via set_k_row), not the 64-line scatter of PR #4898; (b) page_info::k_head_fn returning the row-major row in place (zero copy) and gathering 64 lines only for converted blocks; (c) no conversion of hardware-scored operations' blocks (so the staging never pays the 64-line gather for decode tokens and the main thread does no serial forward-end conversion under FPGA); (d) every reader taking the layout from the block bit, since row-major blocks are permanent and scattered under hardware attention (software loop, staging, copy_from, clear_kv_complete_at); (e) the GOF credit after the stores and wait_for_coop_gof before the scheduler rebuilds gof_jobs; (f) whole-block prefill saves writing VNNI at once, which is the only way a page is dense for the AMX kernel before the engagement point or when DMA lags.

Every K row store and load picks row-major or VNNI (the pair-interleaved layout the AMX kernel reads) from the block bit at call time, row bits are set by the main thread after the shared-window join, and a completed block is converted for every KV head at the forward end (8 KiB of plane traffic per KV head per block, 2.25 MiB per completed block per user for qwen-3-4b, computed from the code). note_k_row_saved can become a transition-detecting fetch_or that is safe with respect to the storing threads (all fetch_or calls on one atomic form a release sequence), but its re-save shortcut path would have to go, and two in-flight readers are not covered by that ordering: the software loop's once-per-visit snapshot of the block mask and the cooperative FPGA staging's in-place row pointer. The per-page state costs 333 bytes for qwen-3-4b (est., computed from the declarations, not measured), stored in the page struct in book::pages, not in the KV planes.

answers.question: (1) The exact per-(page, storage slot) layout state: which bits exist, their types, whether shared across KV heads, plain or atomic
answers.answer: Two masks per (page, storage-slot entry), both std::atomic, both shared by all KV heads of the slot: k_rows_saved_ (std::atomic<uint64_t>, bit o = the K row at page offset o is saved) and k_vnni_blocks_ (std::atomic<uint8_t>, bit c = 16-token block c (offsets 16c..16c+15) holds the VNNI layout; bits 0-3 used). Each array has n_slots + 1 entries: entries 0..n_slots-1 are the logical slots, entry n_slots is the EAGLE storage (used for slot 0 while the EAGLE view is active). A set block bit implies the block's 16 row bits. Row-major slots keep the arrays but never set bits. There is no per-KV-head bit, so one conversion covers all 8 KV heads of qwen-3-4b and a reader must not see the block bit before every head holds the layout.

answers.question: (2) The exact rule of note_k_row_saved and of k_block_to_vnni_at (every KV head; bytes moved)
answers.answer: note_k_row_saved(slot, offset): row-major slot -> false. VNNI slot: relaxed-load the row mask; if the row's bit is clear, fetch_or it (acq_rel); return true iff (mask after | bit) has all 16 bits of the row's block AND the block's converted bit (acquire load) is clear. So it returns true for the row that completes the block, and again for any later re-save of a row of that block while the block waits for its conversion; false once the block is converted. k_block_to_vnni_at(storage, c): returns false unless the 16 row bits of block c are set and the block bit is clear (both acquire loads); otherwise, for every KV head of the storage slot's geometry (8 for qwen-3-4b) it runs block_to_vnni on that head's K plane, then sets the block bit with fetch_or(release) and returns true. block_to_vnni per KV head: 16 memcpy of 256 B from the block to a 4 KiB stack array, then store_block transposes 4 x 16 registers and writes 64 lines of 64 B = 4 KiB back; so 8 KiB of plane traffic (4 KiB read, 4 KiB write) plus 8 KiB of stack traffic per KV head per block, 64 KiB plane traffic per block per slot for 8 KV heads, 2.25 MiB plane traffic per completed block across 36 slots (computed, not measured). The conversion is a serial main-thread loop.

answers.question: (3) set_k_row: how it decides row-major vs VNNI column; what a re-save into a converted block does
answers.answer: set_k_row reads the block's converted bit at call time (k_block_is_vnni, one acquire load) for each (token, KV head) call: bit set -> store_row (4 AVX-512 scatters of 16 dwords into the token's VNNI column); bit clear -> store_row_major (one 256-byte memcpy, 4 whole lines). It never touches the row bits. A re-save into a converted block therefore scatters into the VNNI column, and the following note_k_row_saved returns false (block bit set), so nothing is queued. A re-save into a complete-but-unconverted block writes row-major bytes and note_k_row_saved returns true again (shortcut path, no RMW), so the block is queued a second time; k_block_to_vnni_at converts once and returns false the second time. store_k_block routes every run shorter than 16 tokens through set_k_row and only a 16-token run through set_k_block + note_k_block_saved. In PR 4898 set_k_row always scattered (store_row) and runs of 2..15 tokens used a masked store_block.

answers.question: (4) Every reader and writer of K rows/planes and the layout state, with the calling thread
answers.answer: Writers: (a) save_k on the main thread and, for a minibatch of more than 16 items, the main helpers (shared window): set_k_row / set_k_block per (token, KV head); note_k_block_saved by whichever thread stored the 16-token block; note_k_row_saved only by main after the join, only when !cached_operation_uses_hw; (b) convert_pending_k_blocks -> k_block_to_vnni_at on main at the forward end after run() joined the workers and wait_for_coop_gof drained the staging; (c) clear_kv_complete_at -> k_forget_row on the scheduler thread under the tree lock between passes (child creation full.hpp:669, leaf extension 818, KV-restore invalidation 3346), which may run block_to_rows for every KV head; (d) book::append -> copy_from -> copy_storage_slot (defragmentation, tree lock), running block_to_rows / block_to_vnni and plain stores of both masks; (e) the page move constructor (single-threaded). Readers: (f) the attention software loop on the attention workers: k_vnni_blocks + k_packed once per (page, kv_head) visit, row_major_row for row-major blocks, qk_group for VNNI blocks; (g) the dense AMX page path on the attention workers: k_vnni_blocks == 0xF gate, k_packed into qk_vnni_128x4 (only when amx_q_packed != nullptr, so not under TRON_AMX_DISABLE); (h) FPGA staging k_head_fn inside gof::populate: k_row_if_row_major (in-place pointer) or get_k_row (gather into scratch), on the attention workers (help_drain_gof) during the pass and on main (wait_for_coop_gof) at the forward end, for operations with has_hardware_slot; (i) the EAGLE view: the same accessors with slot 0 resolved to entry n_slots by k_state_ix / k_storage_of; (j) tests: t_k_vnni_layout (save_row_state converts at once, EAGLE view, forget, append), t_llama_unit (mixed pages, hardware-attention sections at 4082/4098), t_amx_dispatch_dtype (record_rows), all single-threaded on the test thread.

answers.question: (5) Could note_k_row_saved be made safe for concurrent callers with an atomic fetch_or, and would 'the thread whose or completes the 16 bits converts' be safe? What needs release/acquire ordering?
answers.answer: The fetch_or itself is already atomic, so concurrent callers for different rows of one block lose no bits. Two changes are needed for a unique converter: (1) completion must be defined as the transition seen in the fetch_or return value, i.e. (before & block_bits) != block_bits && ((before | bit) & block_bits) == block_bits, which exactly one RMW observes; the current 'return true when after has all 16 bits' plus the re-save shortcut (relaxed load, no RMW, returns true for a re-saved row of a pending block) would let a second thread claim the same conversion. (2) The shortcut path must not claim a conversion (a re-saved row then takes store_row_major or store_row per the block bit, as now). Ordering: every storing thread must finish all its KV-head row stores before its fetch_or (the release half of acq_rel covers that); every fetch_or on the same k_rows_saved_[ix] continues one release sequence, so the acquire half of the completing thread's fetch_or synchronizes-with each earlier fetch_or, and all 16 rows' bytes are visible to it before block_to_vnni. The current code already orders bit setting after the row stores (main sets bits after the join, model.hpp:3419-3437; k_rows_saved_ fetch_or is acq_rel). After the transpose the converter must publish with k_vnni_blocks_.fetch_or(release), and readers already load it with acquire (k_vnni_blocks, k_block_is_vnni), so the new bytes are visible to anyone who sees the bit. What that ordering does not cover: readers that decided 'row-major' before the conversion and keep using it: the software loop's per-visit snapshot vnni_blocks and its row_major_row pointer; the FPGA staging's in-place pointer from k_row_if_row_major; and a concurrent set_k_row of a re-saved row of the same block (it picks the layout at call time and then memcpys). The attention workers of the same layer are covered by the upstream_kvs_ready latch (they read a pending page only after every writer minibatch of that page counted down, and a conversion inside save_k would precede the count_down); the cooperative FPGA staging of an earlier minibatch of the same pass is not covered (it reads rows as soon as the GOF is credited), and it can coincide with recorded bits when has_hardware_slot is true but cached_operation_uses_hw is false (sliding-window or scale-mismatch operations, EAGLE). k_forget_row and copy_storage_slot use plain store()/fetch_and and in-place transposes with no lock; they stay safe only because they run between passes under the tree lock. Whether any model of issue 4934 (qwen-3-4b: no sliding window) has a staged-and-recorded operation: Insufficient data.

answers.question: (6) Is there any reader that relies on a block staying row-major until the forward end (other than the hardware staging of hardware-scored ops)?
answers.answer: No reader depends on the forward-end timing as such. The readers depend on the layout not changing during their own visit: the software loop keeps one snapshot of k_vnni_blocks per (page, kv_head) visit and reads row_major_row from it; the FPGA staging keeps an in-place row pointer during gof::populate. Both are satisfied by any conversion point that happens-before the visit. Within a layer the attention workers' visits of a pending page are ordered after every writer minibatch's save_k by the latch. The one in-flight reader the header names is the cooperative FPGA staging of an earlier minibatch of the same pass when a block is split across two minibatches (grains of 8 tokens); that reader exists only for operations that credit GOFs, which can include an operation whose rows are also recorded (predicate mismatch above). The tests convert immediately after note_k_row_saved, so no test relies on deferral. k_forget_row and copy_storage_slot assume no concurrent writer or reader at all (tree lock).

answers.question: (1) For each test case touching the row-major tail block, the conversion timing, the dotters, the live mask or the hardware policy: name, what it asserts, and which of F1-F4 would break it or need a test update.
answers.answer:
Words used here: F1 = no dotters built on the VNNI path, row-major rows scored after the loop by a new AVX-512 routine with the dotter's arithmetic; F2 = conversion inside save_k after the join; F3 = forward-end conversions in parallel on the app pool; F4 = software-scored operations store decode tokens straight into the VNNI column, hardware-scored ones keep the row-major policy.

t_k_vnni_layout.cpp (all [kv_data][k_vnni]):
- 'row-major tail block converts to the VNNI layout and back, bit for bit' (:268). Asserts row_major_row placement (aligned, inside the block's 4 panels, 256 bytes apart) and store_row_major + block_to_vnni == store_row bit for bit, block_to_rows inverts, other blocks untouched. F1/F2/F3: no effect (tensor-level operations stay). F4: still valid because hardware-scored operations keep these operations; no update unless F4 deletes them.
- 'VNNI K reader does not digress from the row-major dotter' (:466). Asserts qk_group vs dotter within 1e-4 x product mass + 1e-6 over prefix, hole and single-token live masks, dead slots keep -inf; all tokens are stored with store_row (no row-major block). F1: does not break it, but F1 needs a sibling case for the new routine (same envelope, or bit-exact if the routine claims the dotter's order). F2/F3/F4: no effect.
- 'page K blocks turn VNNI at the 16th saved row and back when a row is forgotten' (:654, the chain's page-state case). Converts in a test-local helper right after note_k_row_saved (:625-630), so the forward-end timing is not what it tests. Asserts completion only at row 15, block bit from row 15 on, raw bytes of block 1 rows at row_major_row (:714), k_row_if_row_major valid exactly for row-major-block rows (:725-728), forget/re-save transitions. F1/F2/F3: no effect. F4: breaks if set_k_row into an unrecorded block no longer lands at row_major_row bytes or if the block bit gains a new meaning for software-scored slots; the page has one bit set per (page, slot), not per operation policy, so F4 needs a page-state redesign and this case's update.
- 'the EAGLE storage view keeps its own K layout state' (:830), 'forgetting a row acts on every slot's own block' (:906), 'page append carries the K layout state with the rows' (:944). Same helper, same bit semantics. F1/F2/F3: no effect. F4: same as the page-state case.
- The other five cases (index map :109, store/load :128, block save :212, page rows survive store/load/append :525) do not touch the tail block, the timing, the dotters or the policy.

- save_k case (:3851, [kv_data][k_vnni]). answers.question: (3) Which test runs the software loop over a page with a row-major block AND a VNNI block together (mixed page) and checks the scores; if none, say so.
answers.answer: One does: t_llama_unit's 'apply and join page ranges' ([page_range], t_llama_unit.cpp:3203) through check_page_range_reductions. Under TRON_K_VNNI (:2501-2551) it re-stores every page's K with set_k_row and records rows as save_k plus the forward end would: page 0 whole (4 VNNI blocks), every later page rows 0..40 (blocks 0 and 1 VNNI, block 2 a row-major tail of 9 rows, block 3 row-major and unrecorded). The model uses the `host` executor (float activations), so the AMX gate is closed and apply_page_range takes the software loop: qk_group's float path for the VNNI blocks and dotter<float,128> for the row-major rows of the same page. The scores are checked against emulation::compute_attention (s_star and m_star within 1e-5 relative, v_star within 1e-2 absolute / 2e-2 relative, :2740-2758) and the two-way split against the unsplit run (s_star within 1e-6 relative, v_star within 5e-2 under VNNI, :2798-2813). In the uses_hw=false arm (2 pages) page 1 is the mixed page; in the uses_hw=true arm (10 pages) only the last page is software-required and it is mixed. No test checks a mixed page with a bf16 query (the dotter<bf16,128> + qk_group bf16 pairing): t_amx_dispatch_dtype's host_bf16 sections use value-less fakes, and t_k_vnni_layout's reader case has no row-major block.

answers.question: (5) List the test cases by exact Catch2 name for t_k_vnni_layout and the save_k case so a chain script can select them.
answers.answer:
t_k_vnni_layout (all tagged [kv_data][k_vnni]):
1. VNNI K index map matches hand-computed anchors (:109)
2. VNNI K store and load are exact and token-independent (:128)
3. VNNI K block save equals the per-token row store, bit for bit (:212)
4. row-major tail block converts to the VNNI layout and back, bit for bit (:268)
5. VNNI K reader does not digress from the row-major dotter (:466)
6. page K rows survive the store, the load and an append (:525)
7. page K blocks turn VNNI at the 16th saved row and back when a row is forgotten (:654)
8. the EAGLE storage view keeps its own K layout state (:830)
9. forgetting a row acts on every slot's own block (:906)
10. page append carries the K layout state with the rows (:944)
Cases 4, 7, 8, 9, 10 are new in PR #4901.

t_llama_unit save_k case ([kv_data][k_vnni], :3851): save_k stores every token's K row once, grouped by page block, alone or with helper threads. For a Catch2 spec the commas must be escaped: "save_k stores every token's K row once\, grouped by page block\, alone or with helper threads" (as chain2.sh:105 does). Its sections: 'one thread: the grouping stores every row and touches nothing else'; 'hardware attention scores the operation: the completed block stays row-major, the whole-block save is still VNNI'; 'hardware attention scores another operation: this one still converts'; 'three threads: the helpers share the window and every row is stored once'.

Related names a script may need: t_heterogeneous_scheduler 'model::state::forward converts the K block its decode step completes at the forward end' ([attention][k_vnni]); t_amx_dispatch_dtype 'AMX dispatch rejects non-bf16 queries and partial pages' ([amx_numerics][attention]); t_amx_numerics 'AMX QK from the VNNI K plane is bit-identical to AMX QK from row-major K' ([amx_numerics][kv_data]); t_llama_unit 'apply and join page ranges' ([page_range]) and 'software attention compiles for 32 query heads on one 128-dimension K/V head' ([kv_data][k_vnni]).

read:harness.summary: The harness is three layers: build2.sh builds one runtron binary into a /var/tmp/jhan worktree on our half of delphi-3bda, campaign-probe.sh runs the runtron cells (arms mapped by name to RT_BASE/RT_HEAD/RT_NEW/RT_LAZY) and summarize.py reads WEDPERF_ARMS/WEDPERF_PAIRS from the environment, and a detached driver (probe-off.sh, a fork of probe-lazy.sh) takes Bill's marker, takes serving down through platformd, runs the cells and restores serving in its exit handler. Measured costs from the 2026-10-14 pr4off-E-cpu record: takeover 33 s, serving-up 127 s, one run 45 s (tp2 prompt 1024), 103 s AMX-on or 173 s AMX-off (tp2 prompt 8192), 56 to 70 s (tp4 prompt 1024); a 54-run CPU campaign with three AMX-on and three AMX-off arms took 75.2 min on 2026-10-13, an 18-run FPGA campaign 16.6 min, and a fresh runtron-only build 785 s. All four binaries exist on 3bda with sha256 equal to the record header, the shared repo sees 175b1837b9, and /var/tmp has 899 GB free. A fifth binary needs edits at campaign-probe.sh lines 33, 34, 35, 70, 72, 222, 223 and 226 (plus the header), and both campaign-probe.sh and the driver must be forked to new file names because a running script must never be edited over NFS. Only two steps need jhan's order per the script headers: bill-share.sh take and the platformd serving-down; builds and fake-device unit tests run on our half without an order, but the runtron cells cannot run while a rinzler@N unit is active, so they are a whole-machine step.

answers.question: (1) The exact interface of build2.sh
answers.answer: Required env: RES (results dir), SRC (a repo or worktree that has the commit; used only for a fetch when the shared repo lacks it), COMMIT (full sha), WT (/var/tmp/jhan/tron-<name>), SUFFIX, CONFIGURE_ARGS, TARGETS. Optional: TESTS (default none), TEST_ENV, TEST_ARGS, JOBS (default 96; the probes pass 64), OUR_CPUS (default 72-143,216-287), LOG (default $RES/build-$SUFFIX.log). Steps: derive REPO from /var/tmp/jhan/tron-main0916/.git (= /home/jhan/workspace/tron); fetch COMMIT from SRC only when 'git cat-file -e' fails in REPO; 'git worktree add --detach WT COMMIT' when WT/.git is missing, else 'git checkout --detach COMMIT' inside WT; verify HEAD; then nice -n10 taskset -c OUR_CPUS nix develop --command: 'cmake $CONFIGURE_ARGS' (rc 2 = configure-failed) and 'cmake --build gen --target $TARGETS -j$JOBS'; copy gen/runtron to gen/runtron.$SUFFIX when runtron is a target; write $RES/build-$SUFFIX.txt (tip, configure line, cache summary, build seconds, sha256 per target and of runtron.$SUFFIX, --version); run each TESTS binary with SYSTEM_CONFIG="--instance 1,2" (fake device) under timeout 3600 s, writing $RES/tests-$SUFFIX.txt and $RES/tests-$SUFFIX-<t>.out; finally $RES/build-$SUFFIX.done = ok | configure-failed | build-failed rc=N | tests-failed-N | checkout-failed. The binary lands at $WT/gen/runtron.$SUFFIX. A fresh runtron-only build with JOBS=64 took 785 s (13.1 min).

answers.question: (3) The time budget and the schedule windows
answers.answer: Measured 2026-10-14 (pr4off-E-cpu, AMX off): one run (STATUS to next STATUS, about 10 s of it is the guard sample and cleanup) = 45 s at tp2 prompt 1024, 171 to 179 s at tp2 prompt 8192 (prefill alone 117 to 123 s), 56 to 70 s at tp4 prompt 1024. AMX-on runs of tp2 prompt 8192 take 102 to 106 s (pr4-E-cpu, pr4lazy-E-cpu). FPGA-attention runs: 42 to 44 s (tp2 prompt 1024), 55 to 69 s (tp4 prompt 1024). Takeover (start of the driver to STEP 1 with serving down) = 33 s when the engines are idle; dut.sh can poll up to 12 min when traffic persists. Step E of pr4off: 3466 s = 57.8 min for 36 runs; serving-up 127 s; whole driver 60.4 min. The 54-run CPU campaign with 3 AMX-on + 3 AMX-off arms (pr4lazy-E-cpu) took 75.2 min; the 18-run FPGA campaign (pr4-E-fpga) 16.6 min. Windows: the driver's wait_slot (before the build and before step 0) holds while the CI lease is busy (600 s grace), another person is active, or during 02:10-03:45 UTC; END_BY stops a wait and is checked before the whole-machine part and before step E. Inside the campaign, before every run: the 01:40-03:45 UTC pre-CI hold, the lease (no grace) and an active rinzler@N unit block; DEADLINE_HHMM=0130 = 01:30 UTC today or tomorrow, after which the campaign finishes with 'deadline'; a 10 s watcher kills a run when the lease turns busy or a unit comes up. lib-guard: the idle-takeover hold is 01:40-04:30 UTC, a timer starts production at 02:45 UTC and the nightly took the lease at 03:37-03:42 UTC. The scripts do not encode when the nightly ends; the lease file is the authority (status.md estimates a post-CI start of 11:30 to 13:15 UTC).

read:prefill.summary: Prefill under the kill switch (TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1, attn = cpu in every recorded cell) scores every visible (query, page) pair one at a time through apply_page_tok inside apply_page_range's page loop and per-query loop, so an 8192-token prompt makes 528,384 visits per user per layer per KV head (about 1.22e9 visits for 8 users x 36 layers x 8 KV heads). At 8192 tokens every K block is saved whole (runs of 16 in store_k_block), so no row-major tail block, no set_k_row, no pending conversion and no dotter use exists on the prefill path; the diff's prefill-time changes are (i) per visit in the software loop: 4 dotters built, a plane optional plus a block-bit test per relevant token, one k_vnni_blocks load at the first token, and (ii) per save_k on main: a note_k_row_saved call per item (no atomic RMW, the bits are already set by note_k_block_saved) plus one note_k_block_saved and one assert per block. The measured TTFT loss grows 52-113x from prompt 1024 to 8192 while the visit count grows 61x and the token count 8x, so the per-visit loop changes are the leading TTFT suspect (est. 22-43 ns per visit = 27-52 s of worker time per 8-user prefill, 0.45-1.3 s wall for 40-60 workers) and the per-item save_k loop is second (est. 19-35 ms serial). The lazy-dotter probe builds no dotter for any prefill visit at 8192 (no row-major token exists) and did not change TTFT (+21 ms / +100 ms, inside noise), which removes dotter construction as the TTFT cause and leaves the per-token tests and the save_k per-item loop.

answers.question: (1) Is prefill attention computed per query token through apply_page_tok (one (query, page) visit per call), about 8192 x 64.5 page visits per user per layer per KV head? Is there a batched prefill path?
answers.answer: Yes. apply_page_range iterates the pages of its range (self_attention.hpp:1566) and, inside, every query of the minibatch (1597); each query that sees the page calls apply_page_tok once (1640), which scores that one (query, page) pair: the loop over the page's tokens at 2001-2033 builds the live mask, then qk_group scores up to 64 tokens x 4 heads (2045-2048) and the softmax/PV epilogue follows (2054-2080). Queries that do not see the page are skipped at 1612 before the call. There is no batched (multi-query) prefill kernel on the CPU path with AMX off; the AMX dense path (apply_dense_amx_page) is also one (query group, page) per call. Count per user per layer per KV head for 8192 tokens: sum over the 128 pages of (8192 - 64 p) = 528,384 = 8192 x 64.5 visits, 63.5 relevant tokens per visit on average; x 8 KV heads x 36 layers x 8 users = about 1.22e9 visits per 8-user prefill.

answers.question: (2) How many save_k calls and how many items per call does an 8192-token prompt x 8 users produce per layer (chunk size)?
answers.answer: One save_k per minibatch per layer. A forward holds at most 4096 KV token jobs (capacity_limit = ranged_mask_capacity 4096; rinzler default max_minibatches = -1), so each user's prompt is 2 forwards of 4096 tokens and the 8 users take 16 prefill forwards. chunk_evenly cuts 4096 token jobs into ceil(4096 / max_minibatch_size) chunks: with the ingested plugin's max_minibatch_size of 1024 (stated in the comment at self_attention.hpp:1548-1549; the plugin source is outside this repo) that is 4 minibatches of 1024 tokens (64 whole 16-token blocks, 16 pages) per forward, i.e. 4 save_k calls x 1024 items per layer per forward, 64 calls x 1024 items per layer for the whole 8-user prefill (if the plugin used 128, it would be 32 calls x 128 items per forward; the item and block totals do not change). Per layer over the whole prefill: 65,536 items, 4096 whole blocks, 32,768 set_k_block calls (8 KV heads per block), 4096 note_k_block_saved calls, 65,536 note_k_row_saved calls, 65,536 mark_k_complete calls. The store is shared with the main helpers (items > 16), in units of one block.

answers.question: (4) Estimate each item's cost per prefill (est., with units and arithmetic) to rank the TTFT leads.
answers.answer: Counts: 1.217e9 visits, 63.5 relevant tokens per visit, 65,536 saved tokens per layer, 36 layers, 16 forwards. Assumed per-operation costs (est.): a well-predicted branch plus a shift/and/test = 1-2 cycles at about 3.3 GHz = 0.3-0.6 ns; an uncontended acquire load with its index checks = 3-5 ns; a locked fetch_or = 10-20 ns; 16 L1-resident zmm loads = 5-10 ns if not overlapped. (H1) per-visit loop changes in apply_page_tok, attention workers in parallel: first-token fetch 3-5 ns + per-token tests 63.5 x (0.3-0.6) = 19-38 ns -> 22-43 ns per visit x 1.217e9 = 27-52 s of worker time per 8-user prefill; wall time = that / W attention workers (W unknown: Insufficient data); for W = 40-60 this is 0.45-1.3 s, the same order as the measured +0.45-0.59 s. (H2) dotter construction: 5-10 ns per visit = 6-12 s worker time = 0.1-0.3 s wall at W = 40-60, but the lazy probe removed it with no TTFT change (+21/+100 ms, inside noise), so measured, not estimated: about 0 for TTFT. (H4) note_k_row_saved loop on main (serial, after the store join): 65,536 x 36 = 2.36e6 calls x 8-15 ns = 19-35 ms per prefill (4-8 % of the measured delta; scales 8x from p1024, where it would be 2-4 ms against a measured +4..10 ms). note_k_block_saved + assert: 4096 x 36 = 147,456 blocks x 20-40 ns = 3-6 ms per prefill, spread over the store threads. k_forget_row: 65,536 tokens x 37 state entries x 2 ns = about 5 ms per prefill on the scheduler thread. (H3) convert_pending_k_blocks: 16 empty() checks = 0. cached_operation_uses_hw: 2304 calls = 0. Ranking for TTFT: H1 (per-visit loop tests) first, by magnitude and because it is the only item whose p1024 -> p8192 growth (visits x 60.7) matches the measured delta growth (52x-113x); H4 second (19-35 ms); the block bookkeeping and k_forget_row third (3-6 ms, 5 ms); H3 nothing at 8192; H2 excluded by the probe.

answers.question: (5) Is there anything in the prefill path where the row-major tail block matters at 8192 tokens? Confirm from store_k_block's run grouping.
answers.answer: No, when every block is whole. store_k_block groups a run as consecutive items with KV work in the same page and the same 16-token block, stopping at 16 items, a page change, a block change or a repeated offset (model.hpp:3284-3301). Prompt tokens have consecutive positions, each forward holds 4096 tokens (64 pages) from page offset 0 of the user's book, and minibatch boundaries fall at multiples of 1024 (chunk_evenly with grains of 8 and 4 chunks of 1024), so every run has n == 16 and takes the whole-block branch (3303 false -> 3324-3339): set_k_block writes the VNNI layout directly and note_k_block_saved sets the 16 row bits and the block bit. No set_k_row, no row-major block, no pending_k_blocks_ entry, no forward-end conversion, and in the loop every block-bit test at 2024 is true so the dotters are never used. The shared store's unit cut (3207-3230) also cuts at block boundaries, so a helper's unit is one whole block. Caveat: if the harness prompt is not a multiple of 16 tokens (template tokens), the last run of each prompt is partial and that one block per user is stored row-major (store_row_major, 4 whole lines per row) and converted at the end of the forward that saves its 16th row (a decode step); one block per user is negligible for TTFT.

answers.question: (6) Does the lazy-dotter probe remove the dotter construction for prefill page visits too? What does its failure to recover the TTFT eliminate?
answers.answer: Yes. In the probe, dot_q is a std::optional for VNNI slots and is built by 'if (!dot_q) dot_q.emplace(make_dot_q());' inside the row-major else branch (probe self_attention.hpp:1979-1985, 2041). At 8192 prefill there is no row-major token (every block is whole, fact (5)), so no prefill visit builds a dotter under the probe. This eliminates the per-visit dotter construction (16 zmm loads) and the 16 zmm registers held across the loop (the optional lives in memory in the probe) as the TTFT cause. It does not touch, and therefore leaves as the remaining candidates: the per-relevant-token block-bit test and the plane-optional test in the loop (2020-2025), the first-token k_vnni_blocks acquire load, the larger loop body (the else branch's code is still inside the loop), and the save_k-side per-item note_k_row_saved loop (model.hpp:3426-3436) plus the per-block bookkeeping. The probe did recover +1.6 to +2.3 % of decode TPS at tp2, so dotter construction matters for decode visits but not for TTFT.

read:savek.summary: qwen3-4b is an ingested (generated) plugin, so each forward pass runs one minibatch of at most 1024 tokens and save_k is shared with the main helpers only when the minibatch holds more than 16 tokens; a decode step of 8 users is stored by the main thread alone. At ea94e95a4e a decode token costs 4 whole 64-byte lines per KV head (memcpy into the row-major tail block) instead of 64 partial-line scatter writes at dfafd13dce, but PR #4901 adds a serial main-thread loop after the join that runs once per (token, layer) in every pass (1024 iterations per layer, 36,864 per forward pass, 2,359,296 per 8-user 8192-token prefill) and a serial forward-end conversion of every block a step completes (288 queue entries = 2304 block_to_vnni calls = 18 MiB of plane traffic in one step every 16 steps for 8 users at prompt 1024). The block queue is per forward pass, filled across all layers, drained after wait_for_coop_gof on the main thread. cached_operation_uses_hw is a per-operation table filled once in the state constructor; under hardware-scored operations nothing is queued or converted. For the single-minibatch generated plugin I found no reader of a queued block that can be in flight at the join inside save_k: pending-page attention sections wait on a latch that save_k counts down only after the note loop, GOF credits of this pass's tokens happen after the join, and the earlier-minibatch staging hazard the Note names needs several minibatches per pass.

answers.question: (1) Which thread runs each piece?
answers.answer: save_k / save_k_impl worker 0 = the main thread (generated run() passes 0 and n_workers). Helpers = the main helpers: app-pool workers 0..n_main_helpers-1 running run_main_help, which calls save_k with worker_ix 1+i at the same statement position; they wait for their window, claim units, run store_k_block on them, increment `finished` and return. store_k_block runs on whichever thread claimed the unit (main alone when the store is not shared, which is every decode step of 8 users). note_k_block_saved runs on the thread that stored the whole block. The join (main spins on `finished == n_helpers`), the note_k_row_saved loop, pending_k_blocks_.push_back, the mark loop, credit_gof_save and the latch count_down are main-thread only, after the join. Attention workers (the last n_attn_workers pool workers) never call save_k; they run help_drain_gof(4) at each attention operation begin. wait_for_coop_gof and convert_pending_k_blocks run on the main thread after plugin run() returned (run() waits for all helpers and attention workers first).

answers.question: (2) Decode with 8 users: what does store_k_block do per token per KV head at ea94e95a4e vs dfafd13dce?
answers.answer: Both revisions: 8 items form one minibatch (generated plugin, --max-minibatches 1), k_store_shared is false (8 <= 16), so main stores alone, runs of n = 1. ea94e95a4e: set_k_row -> one acquire load of the block bit -> store_row_major = memcpy of 256 bytes = 4 whole 64-byte lines per (token, KV head); 32 whole lines (2 KiB) and 8 atomic loads per token. A row re-saved into an already converted block takes store_row (scatter). dfafd13dce: set_k_row -> store_row = 4 scatters of 16 dwords = 64 writes of 4 bytes into 64 distinct lines per (token, KV head); 512 partial-line writes per token. After the stores, ea94e95a4e adds per token on main: relaxed load + fetch_or (acq_rel, the bit is clear in decode) + acquire load, and every 16th step one vector push_back; the pre-existing mark loop (page_of, offset_in_page, mark_k_complete fetch_add, GOF credit) is unchanged.

answers.question: (3) The note_k_row_saved loop in an 8-user x 8192-token prefill: iterations per layer and per forward pass, chunking, cost per iteration, note_k_block_saved per block, per-prefill count.
answers.answer: Chunking: there is no TRON_CHUNK_SIZE; the pass size is the scheduler's live-token limit = max_minibatches x max_minibatch_size = 1 x 1024 for an ingested plugin (TRON_LIVE_TOKEN_LIMIT and the 4096 hard cap are larger), so a pass holds one minibatch of 1024 tokens (documented as 128 per user). Note loop: 1024 iterations per layer per pass, 36 x 1024 = 36,864 per forward pass, 64 passes, 2,359,296 for the prefill. Each iteration: token_jobs_do_kv read, token_jobs read, page_of (pointer table lookup), offset_in_page (integer subtraction), note_k_row_saved = k_state_ix (eagle check) + relaxed load of the row bits + fetch_or only when the bit is clear (never in a whole-block prefill, since note_k_block_saved already set the 16 bits) + acquire load of the block bits; returns false for a block-saved row, so no push_back. note_k_block_saved: once per whole block on the storing thread, two fetch_or; 4096 blocks per layer, 147,456 per prefill, spread over main and helpers. The mark loop runs the same 2,359,296 iterations at both revisions. Per-iteration time in ns: Insufficient data (needs a TSC or perf measurement of the loop).

answers.question: (4) When does save_k run relative to this layer's attention readers; could a block be converted right after the join inside save_k; which readers of K rows could be in flight?
answers.answer: Order in the generated pass: launch_early_hw_attention, save_k, save_v, prepare_late_hw_attention, launch_late_hw_attention. The layer's attention workers may already be running READY sections (pages not written this pass) during save_k; PENDING sections (pages written this pass, where every queued block lives) wait on upstream_kvs_ready[slot], which save_k counts down only at its very end (after the note loop and the mark loop) and save_v counts down after its stores; the single minibatch is its own producer (page-wide token_ix_needed). Readers that can be in flight at the join: attention workers on ready pages (no queued block there); attention workers inside help_drain_gof doing GOF staging (reads rows in place through k_row_if_row_major), but a GOF of this pass's tokens is credited only after the join (mark loop of save_k, then save_v), and earlier passes' GOFs were drained by wait_for_coop_gof at the previous forward end; main helpers (writers only, returned); other layers' workers (other kv_slots); page copies / clear_kv_complete_at (between passes, tree lock). So for the single-minibatch generated plugin I found no reader that a conversion right after the join (before count_down) could corrupt. The Note's reason for deferring (an earlier minibatch's GOF staging reading a block whose last rows a later minibatch saves) needs several minibatches per pass, i.e. the handwritten llama.hpp plugin. The ordering constraint that remains: the conversion must come after the join (helpers' stores happen-before main's acquire of `finished`), and it is serial main-thread work placed before the pending sections can start, so it would add to the critical path the Note names.

answers.question: (5) convert_pending_k_blocks: per block, what is read and written, on which thread, is it serial, burst or spread, queue per pass or per layer?
answers.answer: Per queue entry (one page, one storage slot, one block): two acquire loads, a compile-time loop over the active slots for the geometry, then for each of 8 KV heads block_to_vnni = 4 KiB plane read into a 4 KiB stack buffer (16 memcpy of 256 B), then store_block = 64 loads of 64 B from the stack, 4 transposes, 64 full-line stores to the plane (4 KiB written); then one release fetch_or. Per entry: 32 KiB plane read, 32 KiB plane written, 32 KiB stack write + 32 KiB stack read. Main thread, plain serial for loop, after wait_for_coop_gof. With 8 users at prompt 1024 and equal step counts, all 8 users complete a block in the same step, every 16th step: 288 entries (8 users x 36 layers) = 2304 block_to_vnni calls = 18 MiB of plane traffic (9 MiB read + 9 MiB written) plus 18 MiB of stack traffic in that one forward end; the other 15 steps convert nothing. The queue is one member vector per model state, filled by every layer's save_k of the pass and cleared at the forward end: per pass, not per layer. Under a hardware-scored operation nothing is queued.

answers.question: (6) Is cached_operation_uses_hw a per-operation static decision or can it change per minibatch/pass?
answers.answer: Static per operation: it returns attention_operation_uses_hw[op.i], a table filled once in the state constructor by cache_attention_operation_hardware_eligibility (right after configure_hw_attention) from compute_operation_uses_hw, which depends on is_eagle, hw_attn_eligible, the hardware-candidate geometry test, the scale and the sliding window. Nothing rewrites the table per minibatch or pass. The per-pass hardware plan can still leave an eligible operation to software (before the 127-token engagement point, empty plan); those blocks then stay row-major and are scored with the dotter, by design.

answers.question: (7) What is k_storage_of / k_storage_ref and why is it captured at the save?
answers.answer: k_storage_ref = {kv_storage_offset offset, size_t state_ix}: the physical storage slot behind a logical slot and the index of its layout-state entry (the extra EAGLE entry when the EAGLE view maps slot 0 onto the EAGLE storage). k_storage_of(slot) resolves this under the current view. save_k stores the resolved pair in the queue entry so that a view change between the save and the forward end cannot redirect the conversion to another storage; k_block_to_vnni_at addresses the planes with storage.offset and the bits with state_ix.

read:loop.summary: On the kill-switch path (TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1, the AMX kernels off inside the same binary) every (query, page) visit of apply_page_tok runs the software loop, and PR #4901's loop adds two kinds of work that PR #4898's loop did not have: per visit, it builds 4 dotters (dotter<bf16,128>, the per-token dot product over one row-major K row) with 16 aligned 512-bit loads of the same 1024 bytes of q that the AVX-512 reader k_vnni::qk_group reads anyway, and per relevant token it tests a std::optional and a block bit before setting the live bit. The dotters are built even when no token of the page is row-major, which is the case for every page but the newest one of a user. The tail rows are scored by the dotter with a different fp32 add order than qk_group (two accumulators over 32-dimension chunks, a lane-wise add, then a 16-lane horizontal reduction), so a token's score changes add order when its block converts; the epilogue after the loop does not care which path wrote a score. Prefill and decode go through the same per-(query, page) call with no batched software path, so an 8192-token software prefill pays the per-visit cost on the order of 10^8 times (est.). The probe ca6456b7dc defers the dotter build to the first row-major token, and its comment is wrong: dotter<bf16,128> copies q as bf16 and converts nothing at construction.

A bit-identical replacement must keep: the two accumulators with this chunk-to-accumulator assignment, each started from zero, the lane-wise add, and the same reduce_sum helper on the same lane vector. The products inside VDPBF16PS are the instruction's own (bf16 x bf16 into fp32); the repository documents them as exact products added in fp32.

This is the same instruction the row-major dotter<bf16, 128> uses. Only the order of the fp32 adds differs".

facts.claim: qk_group's add order for a bf16 query differs from the dotter's: one accumulator per head, 64 chained VDPBF16PS per token lane in dimension-pair order (step 0..3, pair 0..15), no lane-wise add and no horizontal reduction. The repository states that a score, and so a generated token, can differ by this add order alone. Consequence in PR #4901: a tail token is scored by the dotter until its block converts at the forward end, and by qk_group afterwards, so its score's add order changes across the conversion. facts.claim: Call structure: apply_page_range loops over the pages of its section and, inside each page, over the queries q_begin..q_end of the minibatch, and calls apply_page_tok once per (query, page). The packed Q group is produced once per token per call at its first page. answers.answer: The same per-(query, page) call. apply_page_range loops over the section's pages (line 1566) and inside each page over the batch's queries q_begin..q_end (line 1597), calling apply_page_tok once per (query, page) at line 1640. The `items` list is the batch's token jobs whether they are prompt tokens or decode tokens (run_sections, lines 1170-1172), so a prefill query visits each of its visible pages one at a time; there is no batched software QK over several queries. answers.question: (4) Does the dense AMX gate return before the dotters are built with AMX on?
answers.answer: Yes. The gate `amx_q_packed != nullptr && is_dense_amx_page(...) && k_layout_dense()` at lines 1932-1935 and its `return` at line 1942 come before `s_pages` (line 1946) and the dotter array (lines 1969-1974). So with AMX on, a dense page whose 4 blocks are VNNI never builds dotters; the dotter cost is paid only by software-visited pages: partial pages, pages with a row-major block (the newest page of a user in decode, until its block converts at the forward end), and pages outside the gate. The k_layout_dense lambda is evaluated only when the first two gates hold (short-circuit &&); on the AMX-on path it adds one k_state_ix and one 1-byte acquire load per dense visit, which PR #4898 did not have.

answers.question: (6) The numerics of the row-major dotter<bf16,128>::dot, precisely, for a bit-identical replacement.
answers.answer: Construction: x01, x23, x45, x67 = the four aligned 512-bit loads of the query head row (bf16 dims 0-31, 32-63, 64-95, 96-127), kept as bf16. dot(K row): y01..y67 = the four aligned 512-bit loads of the K row (same dimension chunks). sum1 = VDPBF16PS(zero, x01, y01): 16 fp32 lanes, lane j = q[2j]*k[2j] + q[2j+1]*k[2j+1] for dims 0-31. sum2 = VDPBF16PS(zero, x23, y23) for dims 32-63 (lane j covers dims 32+2j, 32+2j+1). sum1 = VDPBF16PS(sum1, x45, y45) for dims 64-95. sum2 = VDPBF16PS(sum2, x67, y67) for dims 96-127. Then `sum1 + sum2` = one lane-wise VADDPS on __m512 (fp32x16 converts through operator __m512), then reduce_sum(fp32x16) = _mm512_reduce_add_ps, whose lane order is the compiler's (clang-19 in the presets; its header is not installed on this machine, so the exact tree is Insufficient data here). A bit-identical replacement must: start each accumulator from zero, assign chunks 0 and 2 to accumulator 1 and chunks 1 and 3 to accumulator 2 in that order, use VDPBF16PS (the same instruction, with its own bf16 x bf16 product and fp32 add semantics), do the single lane-wise add sum1 + sum2, and call the same reduce_sum helper on that lane vector. The 4 heads are independent dot calls; their order does not matter. The per-token result is stored as one float into s_pages[head][i]. The reader qk_group uses a different order (one accumulator per head, 64 chained VDPBF16PS per token lane in dimension-pair order, no horizontal reduction), and the repository documents that the two orders can differ by rounding and change a generated token.

The attention workers of another minibatch cannot read a block being completed either: token_ix_needed is page-granular (a consumer minibatch depends on every producer of any page one of its queries sees [common.hpp:1068-1082; model.hpp:2008-2027]), the pending sections wait on upstream_kvs_ready[slot] [self_attention.hpp:821-823], and save_k counts that latch down only after the recording loop and mark_k_complete [model.hpp:3419-3455]. [design_critical] credit_gof_save is gated on has_hardware_slot = (geometry == hardware_geometry && operation_is_hardware_candidate(operation)) [model.hpp:3370-3372, :3497-3499], not on cached_operation_uses_hw or slot_uses_hw. A fix must not read has_hardware_slot as 'the hardware scores this operation'.

[design_critical] Under FPGA decode the software tail per (user, layer, KV head) is bounded by the GOF: the single-query entry boundary is the last DMA-complete GOF, dma_last_abs = base_tok_ix + complete_prefix_gofs * 4 - 1 [full.hpp:2874-2880 first shard, :2906-2919 partial leaf shard; gof_tokens = 4 at gof.hpp:34], and the first shard is pushed only after hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload = 32 GOFs = 128 tokens [h/pos/config.hpp:98] and above position 127 [libpos.hpp:90]. So every decode step scores at least 1 and normally at most 4 tail tokens plus the DMA lag (est., not measured) in software, all in the newest page. Decode-saved rows under a hardware-scored operation stay row-major forever (claim 8), prefill whole-block rows are VNNI (claim 17): a page is permanently MIXED under FPGA. A fix that removes the per-token layout test cannot assume a page-uniform layout under FPGA; it needs the per-page block mask (k_vnni_blocks, 4 bits per (page, slot) [kv_cache.hpp:2131-2137]) or must convert under hardware too, which would re-introduce the 64-line gather in k_head_fn [full.hpp:2766-2767] that PR #4901 removed for issue #4500.

The tail move of full.hpp:2050-2061 runs only for multi-query entries ('if (entry.query_mask.count() <= 1) continue;' [full.hpp:2050]). Decode entries (one query per user) take their HW/SW boundary from the shard push position instead [full.hpp:2874-2880]. A reader of the 2036-2061 block alone would overestimate how the decode tail is produced.

[design_critical] Under USE_HW_ATTN=0 nothing of the hardware path runs inside forward: no shards [full.hpp:2489-2490], no GALs or GOFs [:2667], empty hw_plan_entries [:2069-2072], null gof_rodeo_fn and empty gof_jobs_span [:2074-2083], credit_gof_save returns at :3552, no dma_tracker (created only in the enabled branch [model.hpp:1604]), help_drain_gof finds an empty queue [:3570-3576], wait_for_coop_gof is one failed try_dequeue and one load [:3583-3592]. The measured kill-switch loss therefore comes entirely from the software side: the per-token recording loop (one locked fetch_or per token per layer [kv_cache.hpp:2179-2180]), the serial main-thread conversion (288 block_to_vnni calls per user per 16 decode steps for qwen-3-4b, 4.5 MiB est. of traffic [kv_cache.hpp:744-749; :2228-2232]), the dotter construction per (page, KV head) visit [self_attention.hpp:1969-1974], and the per-token bit test [:2024].

[design_critical] What a fix must keep to preserve PR #4901's FPGA gains (issue #4500): (a) decode rows of a hardware-scored slot stored as 4 whole lines, store_row_major [k_vnni.hpp:487-491], chosen by set_k_row on the block bit [kv_cache.hpp:2254-2258]; (b) k_head_fn returning the row in place through k_row_if_row_major for a row-major block [full.hpp:2762-2765; kv_cache.hpp:2334-2350]; (c) no conversion of those blocks (no row bit, no queue) [model.hpp:3425; kv_cache.hpp:731-749], so the staging never pays the 64-line gather. The software loop's dotter path for the FPGA tail [self_attention.hpp:2024-2031] is the only CPU scoring those rows get, so a fix that makes decode blocks VNNI again under hardware would move the FPGA staging back to get_k_row (64 lines per row) for every decode GOF.

Under FPGA with every operation hardware-scored, convert_pending_k_blocks returns at its first line on every pass [model.hpp:3176-3177]; in a model with software-scored operations beside hardware ones (a sliding-window operation fails both predicates [model.hpp:1561-1562; self_attention.hpp:514-516]), those operations do queue blocks and the forward-end conversion runs for them while the FPGA path is active. The staging never reads their slots (no GOF created), so even there the deferral protects nothing (see the forward-end fact above).

USE_HW_ATTN=N (N > 0) raises the engagement point to k * 64 - 1 (rounded up to a page boundary, floor 127) [hw_attn_config.cpp:26-31; hw_attn_config.hpp:18-23]. Below that position a hardware-scored operation is CPU-scored with the row-major dotter for every decode-completed block and never becomes AMX-dense [kv_cache.hpp:755-764]. Any kill-switch-only fix leaves this cell unchanged.

In gof::populate the V side always unpacks into the 256-byte scratch (v_head_fn -> get_v) [full.hpp:2775-2786; gof.cpp:216-219]; only the K callback changed between the PRs (claim 10). A fix on the K layout does not touch the V staging cost.

design_critical=true. design_critical=true. design_critical=true. In prefill, a block is stored row-major only when a run is shorter than 16: the prompt's last partial block, or a block cut by a minibatch boundary. Whether the issue's 8192-token prefill produces such boundaries is Insufficient data (it needs the chunk sizes of a run; max_minibatch_size is 128 in llama.hpp:184 and 1024 for ingested plugins per self_attention.hpp:1549-1550).

design_critical=true. For decode that is users x layers locked RMWs per step on the main thread, serial, after the join. Not measured here; the attention stats (TRON_ATTN_STATS) or a perf counter on the engine pid would show whether it is visible.

design_critical=false. missed: [design_critical=true] Admission order, not a per-user split, decides the per-pass shares. compute_forward_args is a post-order DFS over the token tree [full.hpp:2232-2245] and the edge loop admits KV tokens of one edge until n_live_tokens reaches live_token_limit = 1024 [full.hpp:2332-2337]; no code divides the 1024 tokens among users. The Note's '128 tokens of each user per pass' [model.hpp:3092-3093] is a measurement description with no mechanism in the scheduler I could find (Insufficient data: a trace with the per-pass 'Save K' item counts would show the real split). Consequence for the burst (claim 12): per completing user 36 entries (2.25 MiB plane traffic) at that user's step, spread over the steps the users' phases fall on.

[design_critical=true] The conversion sits on the step's critical path with the whole pool idle: run_forward calls plugin_state.run (which joins every helper and attention worker, Note [Plugin-owned worker launch], model.hpp:1826-1829), then wait_for_coop_gof, then convert_pending_k_blocks, and only then launches logit delivery on the pool [model.hpp:1836-1854]. Every block_to_vnni of a pass therefore runs serially on main while all app-pool workers wait, and delays the logits of that step. A design that spreads the entries over the pool at the forward end, or converts on the attention workers that already read the block in the completing step, changes this.

[design_critical=true] On a run without hardware attention the deferral reason is absent: gof_jobs_span is set only when hw_attn_eligible and gof_jobs is non-empty, else it is empty and gof_rodeo_fn is null [full.hpp:2074-2082]; credit_gof_save then returns at `if (ix.i >= gof_jobs_span.size()) return;` [model.hpp:3552] and wait_for_coop_gof finds an empty queue [model.hpp:3583-3591]. With one minibatch per pass (generated plugin) and no GOF staging, the only reader of a completed block during the pass is the pending section of the same layer, which waits on the latch counted down after the note loop [model.hpp:3453-3455]. So a conversion inside save_k after the join (before the mark loop) has no concurrent reader in the issue's software-attention configuration; the Note's hazard [kv_cache.hpp:691-697] needs several minibatches per pass.

[design_critical=true] Where the kill switch bites: nothing in save_k, the note loop or convert_pending_k_blocks checks TRON_AMX_DISABLE (grep of model.hpp finds no AMX switch in the save path); the Note says 'The kill switch keeps the layout. With TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 a TRON_K_VNNI binary runs the AVX-512 VNNI reader, not the row-major dotter' [kv_cache.hpp:818-822]. So under the kill switch PR #4901 pays the row-major store, the note loop, the dotter scoring of the tail rows in the completing step, and the forward-end conversion, and gains qk_group only from the next pass on; at dfafd13dce the kill-switch run scored every token of a partial page with qk_group at once. The AMX-on run differs only in the dense page path [self_attention.hpp:1924-1932], which neither revision takes for a partial page.

[design_critical=true] The completing step scores the fresh block with the row-major dotter, and each dotter is built per (page, KV head) visit: self_attention.hpp:1966-1972 (ea94e95a4e) constructs kv_mul = 4 dotter<bf16,128> objects, each loading the 256-byte query row into 4 zmm registers [h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp:174-200], before the token loop; the per-token dot is 4 dpbf16 plus a horizontal reduce_sum [dotter.hpp:214-224], where qk_group keeps one token per lane and needs no reduction [kv_cache.hpp:784-792]. The probe ca6456b7dc (worktree P, self_attention.hpp only) defers that construction to the first row-major token (`std::optional`, `if (!dot_q) dot_q.emplace(make_dot_q())`), which removes the construction for pages with no row-major block. This is the attention subsystem, listed because the savek design (when to convert) decides how many rows reach the dotter.

[design_critical=false] New per-step bookkeeping in decode at ea94e95a4e versus dfafd13dce: per (token, layer) one relaxed load plus one locked fetch_or (acq_rel) on k_rows_saved_ in the note loop [kv_cache.hpp:2179-2180] = 8 x 36 = 288 locked read-modify-writes per 8-user step, and per (token, KV head, layer) one acquire load of k_vnni_blocks_ in set_k_row [kv_cache.hpp:2256, 2516-2520] = 2304 loads per step; none of these existed in the old set_k_row -> store_row path [old kv_cache.hpp:2018-2028]. The diff of model.hpp shows no other hot-path change (the note loop is the only insertion inside save_k_impl).

[design_critical=true] Users do not necessarily start at page offset 0: kv_location_for_tokens continues the parent's book at `parent_edge.kv_last_entry_nr() + 1` for a node's first child, and allocates a new book (entry 0) otherwise [full.hpp:1017-1037]. A decode token is the prompt node's first child, so it continues the prompt's pages (prompt 1024 -> page 16 offset 0). With runtron's --shared-system-prompt-length [src/runtron.cpp:1032], the first user's own prompt continues the system prompt's book mid-page while the other users start new books at offset 0; a system prompt length that is not a multiple of 16 then makes that user's prefill shares end inside blocks (row-major tails plus a forward-end conversion in every prefill pass of that user) and puts its decode block completions at a different phase from the others.

[design_critical=false] Duplicate queue entries are possible and cheap: note_k_row_saved returns true again for a row re-saved into a complete, unconverted block [kv_cache.hpp:2165-2167, 2181-2185], so pending_k_blocks_ can hold the same block twice; the second k_block_to_vnni_at returns CONVERTED_FALSE after two acquire loads [kv_cache.hpp:2221-2225]. k_block_to_vnni_at does not check k_storage_readable; it relies on the page's storage being resident at the forward end of the same pass.

[design_critical=false] Measurement hooks already exist for the two hypotheses: TRACE_EVENT('model', 'convert_k_blocks', 'blocks', n) [model.hpp:3178] records the entry count and duration of every forward-end burst, and TRACE_EVENT('model', 'Save K') [model.hpp:3367] brackets each layer's save including the note loop; a Perfetto trace of the issue's cells separates the burst cost from the per-layer save cost without new code.
